entry.title: 🚀 5 Must-Know Modern JavaScript Tips for Cleaner Code
Inside the Critical Rendering Path: What Your Browser Is Really Doing
entry.summary:
When you visit a web page, a lot happens before you see anything. Bytes travel, files load, scripts run—and somewhere in that flurry of activity, pixels appear on your screen. That journey is called the Critical Rendering Path (CRP). It’s the behind-the-scenes choreography that turns code into content, and understanding it is key to diagnosing and improving how users experience your site. What Is the Critical Rendering Path?
The CRP is the sequence of steps the browser follows to convert HTML, CSS, and JavaScript into pixels. These steps include: HTML parsing → DOM construction CSS parsing → CSSOM construction DOM + CSSOM → Render Tree creation Render Tree → Layout (calculating element positions) Layout → Paint (rasterizing pixels on screen) Each of these phases depends on network respon…

entry.title: What is Tails OS?
entry.summary:
Introduction
What if I told you... you could disappear from the internet? No data. No logs. No tracking. No history. A full operating system that leaves ZERO TRACE every time you shut it down. This... is Tails OS—the privacy freak's shield, the hacker’s weapon, and the government’s worst nightmare. What Is Tails OS?
Tails OS is a privacy-focused live operating system based on Debian Linux. It was first released on June 23, 2009, by The Tails Project, a non-profit organization dedicated to digital privacy. Unlike traditional operating systems, Tails boots directly from a USB stick, turning any computer into a temporary, secure, privacy-dedicated machine. And when you shut it down?
